rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise concerning later generations resembles the glad tidings in al-Mumtahinah 60:7.
rows.anchor: future are similar to the glad tidings in verse seven of S ūrah al-Mumtahinah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can guide all mankind through His might, but His wisdom means He guides only those worthy of guidance.
rows.anchor: if He wants, He can bless all mankind with guidance because He is Mighty; however, He is also wise

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” refers to the great blessing God had bestowed on the unlettered Arabs and mentioned earlier.
rows.anchor: This is a reference to the great blessing

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God chooses the recipients of His favour according to His wisdom; no one can claim an exclusive right to it or interfere in that choice.
rows.anchor: He chooses those people whom He desires, to be the recipients of His favour, and no one can have monopoly over His favour

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews’ jealousy is misplaced: the favour belongs to God, so their anger can harm only themselves, not its recipients.
rows.anchor: The Almighty has bestowed the ummiyyīn with something which belongs to Him, and not which belongs to someone else, that they should express anger.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The donkey laden with books rebuts the Jews’ arrogant claim that only they can receive the sharī‘ah: they carry scripture without understanding it.
rows.anchor: Their example is that of a donkey who is carrying the burden of books but has no idea what is written in them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though entrusted with the Torah, the Jews did not follow its teachings; they thereby forfeited its reward and carried sin instead.
rows.anchor: they did not continue to profess faith in the teachings and directives of the Torah. They denied them practically.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for bearing the Torah hints that it was imposed on the Jews rather than accepted eagerly; al-Baqarah discusses this imposition, and al-Ṣaff 61:5 recalls Moses’ grief at their resistance.
rows.anchor: its burden was in fact imposed on them by force.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who set such a bad example should not regard themselves as God’s chosen intimates or assume He would entrust His law to no one else.
rows.anchor: it is not befitting for people who are such bad examples, to regard themselves to be the chosen and near ones of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews cannot be Torah’s trustees while denying its directives in practice and failing to follow it.
rows.anchor: They do claim that they are its recipients; but if they do not follow it in practice, how can they be regarded as its trustees?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning that God does not guide wrongdoers also occurs at 61:7; their misdeeds have brought condemnation and sealed hearts, and they compound their rejection of the Torah by rejecting the final Messenger.
rows.anchor: They denied the Torah bestowed upon them, and now in their conceited claim of being its custodians, they are denying the last Messenger of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Jews truly were nearest to God, they would long to meet Him and not evade death; their fear exposes their claim.
rows.anchor: The lover is the most desirous of meeting his beloved. He does not evade what leads him to his beloved.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥashr portrays Banū Qurayẓah and their allies as so fearful that they will not fight openly and fear the Muslims more than God.
rows.anchor: fear you more than they fear God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqarah develops the same challenge: the Jews will not wish for death because of their misdeeds and instead are exceptionally greedy for life.
rows.anchor: In Sūrah al-Baqarah, this subject is discussed thus in relatively more detail:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although “others” is general, it particularly means the Ishmaelites, toward whom Jewish hostility arose from Torah predictions and racial jealousy and intensified when Muḥammad appeared.
rows.anchor: Because of the predictions of the Torah and because of racial jealousy, the Jews had special enmity with them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews stayed silent because the challenge struck a sore point that their past and present conduct confirmed.
rows.anchor: so they sought refuge in silence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their misdeeds are the reason they are too cowardly to wish for death.
rows.anchor: Mentioned in this verse is the reason of their cowardice; what has made them so

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their misdeeds include killing prophets, altering the Torah, betraying God’s trust, and concealing signs they were responsible for making known; they will face punishment when they meet God.
rows.anchor: they have killed prophets of God, interpolated the Torah and have been dishonest in what they have been entrusted by God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death will catch those fleeing it; they will appear before God, who knows the hidden and manifest, and be shown and punished for all their deeds.
rows.anchor: if they want to run away from death, they should try doing so – but where can they run? It will overtake them one day

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A caravan arrived in Madīnah, and some people left the mosque during the Prophet’s Friday sermon to go to it; although a few acted this way, the incident exposed weaknesses in the whole community.
rows.anchor: A trade caravan once entered Madī nah. When some people heard of this news, they left the mosque

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The incident showed that many Muslims did not appreciate God’s great blessing in sending Muḥammad to the unlettered Arabs.
rows.anchor: many people were not fully cognizant of the great blessing of God which He bestowed on the unlettered Arabs

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second weakness was failure to absorb al-Ṣaff 61:10–13: those who pledged to listen and obey sold their lives and wealth for forgiveness and Paradise, so they must not prefer commerce to the Messenger’s sermon.
rows.anchor: people who had made a covenant of “to listen and to obey” with the Prophet (sws), had sold out their lives and wealth to God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the address targets those rebuked for weak character, addressing believers generally avoids humiliating them; the upright can accept the gentle advice, while pointed rebuke risks stubbornness and pride.
rows.anchor: The benefit of a general address is that the people who are actually addressed do not feel humiliated

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “on Friday” specifies that the prayer is the Friday prayer, the distinctive prayer of that day.
rows.anchor: It is solely the prayer which distinguishes this day from the rest.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third weakness was not recognizing Friday’s sanctity: as the Israelites incurred God’s curse and disfigurement by violating the Sabbath for worldly pleasures, Muslims could also incur divine wrath by profaning Friday.
rows.anchor: This day is similar to what Saturday was to the Israelites.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These grave weaknesses led Muslims to undervalue the blessing given to Arabia’s unlettered people, a blessing emphasized throughout the sūrah and resented by the Jews.
rows.anchor: All these weaknesses were very grave
